selected_evidence.requirement: Single named port-object (alias) created on node1 for ports 8080/8443/9000
selected_evidence.summary: Python config.xml edit added alias 'node3_svc_ports' (type=port, content=8080/8443/9000); post-restart dump confirms alias persisted with correct content.

selected_evidence.requirement: Single firewall rule referencing the alias instead of one rule per port
selected_evidence.summary: pfctl -sr shows one rule (single label) expanded by pf into three port matches from the alias, both before and after node1's restart.

selected_evidence.requirement: node2 permitted to reach node3 on TCP 8080, 8443, 9000
selected_evidence.summary: socat listeners started on node3; node2 connect attempts succeeded on 8080/8443/9000 only after also opening node3's local firewalld ports (a separate OS-level firewall).

selected_evidence.requirement: Rule scoped only to the specified ports (negative control)
selected_evidence.summary: Connection to unlisted port 2222 timed out from node2->node3, and node3->node2 (reverse direction) also timed out, confirming default-deny still applies outside the alias.
Captured kern.boottime baseline; pf rules/interfaces verified healthy pre- and functionally re-verified post-restart.

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
selected_evidence.summary: SSH reboot command closed the connection (ack); subsequent poll timed out then succeeded with a new kern.boottime (16:24:15 -> 16:32:13); interfaces, pf rule, and ip forwarding confirmed recovered.

selected_evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
selected_evidence.summary: Reboot command dropped the exec stream (ack); poll timed out then returned a new boot_id/uptime -s; eth1 IP and routes confirmed persisted via nmcli.

selected_evidence.requirement: node3 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
selected_evidence.summary: Reboot command dropped the exec stream (ack); poll timed out then returned a new boot_id/uptime -s; eth1 IP, routes, and firewalld ports confirmed persisted.

selected_evidence.requirement: Post-restart end-to-end functional re-verification of the alias-based policy
selected_evidence.summary: After all three nodes restarted, fresh listeners on node3 and connect attempts from node2 confirmed 8080/8443/9000 still reachable end-to-end through the surviving alias/rule/routing configuration.
